assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and related molecular sieves with controlled pores, framework topology and active sites underpins petrochemical refining, selective catalysis and emissions control. Structure-directing agents, new frameworks and high-silica chabazite-type catalysts show a clear route from synthesis to function. From a structural-chemistry view, solving these frameworks depended on crystallography at the limit of crystal size.
assessment.attribution: Corma (catalyst design and industrial zeolite catalysis), Davis (framework and SDA design, chiral and extra-large-pore materials) and Zones (SDA-directed synthesis, SSZ-13 and related materials) cover the field's synthesis-to-application arc. Tsapatsis and Jihong Yu are also strong; the field is broad enough that a three-person cut is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and sustained industrial use. Timely, and recognition would sit near the 2025 prize for framework materials without duplicating it.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as one coherent discovery or a broad field with many contributors.
Overlap in the committee's mind with the 2025 MOF prize and older zeolite-related awards.
My own field closeness means I should discount my enthusiasm; the supplied text does not settle relative credit among Corma, Davis and Zones.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one DNA base to another without double-strand breaks, a new molecular-level tool that works at the nucleotide level and has reached clinical trials. The concept is original and chemically defined (deaminase fused to a Cas variant).
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu led the invention and the evolution of cytosine and adenine editors; Komor and Gaudelli did key work as his trainees. Nishida and Kondo made a parallel cytosine-editing report. A single-laureate award is plausible, but the parallel work and the neighbouring prime-editing candidate complicate the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent adoption and first clinical use within about ten years. Probably timely, though clinical outcome evidence is still accumulating and the Chemistry-versus-Medicine placement is a question.
uncertainties: Whether the Chemistry committee will treat genome editing as chemistry after CRISPR in 2020.
Credit split with Nishida and Kondo on the first cytidine-deaminase editor.
Overlap with prime editing (B068) as a related Liu invention.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites rapidly reached high solar cell efficiency and opened a new class of tunable semiconductors. Impact on photovoltaics research has been very large and clear.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cell; Park and Snaith made decisive steps in solid-state devices and efficiency, with Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also notable. Priority and credit are contested and any three-person selection will leave out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Wide independent replication and a very active field. Stability and commercial scale-up remain open, so recognition may be somewhat early for the application but not for the discovery.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among six names is unresolved.
Long-term stability and toxicity concerns.
Whether the discovery is chemistry or materials physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silicas (MCM-41, SBA-15 and relatives) created periodic mesopores with tunable size, a foundational advance for porous solids and nanostructured materials. The materials were also a testing ground for electron crystallography of porous materials.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck (Mobil) did the MCM-41 discovery, while Stucky (SBA-15) and Ryoo (carbon replication, ordered mesoporous carbons) extended the approach. Beck's role and the Japanese FSM-16 work by Inagaki complicate a three-person list.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of independent work. Recognition is overdue rather than premature, though application impact has been smaller than for zeolites.
uncertainties: Priority between Mobil and Japanese FSM-16 work.
Applied impact is more modest than the scientific influence.
Choice of three from six credited names is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis is a general platform for radical chemistry in organic synthesis, now widely used in medicinal chemistry. It is a substantial, clear conceptual advance.
assessment.attribution: Yoon, Stephenson and Nicewicz independently introduced photoredox catalysis for synthetic transformations in 2008-2011, alongside MacMillan, who is already a laureate (2021 organocatalysis). The attribution is therefore awkward and could favor others on the list such as Melchiorre and König.
assessment.maturity: Very strongly confirmed and broadly adopted. The prior MacMillan prize makes the timing and attribution more complicated.
uncertainties: Prior recognition of MacMillan, whose name appears in the supplied credit list, and a possible sense that the field was partly honored in 2021.
Unclear which three contributors best capture the core idea.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography with X-ray free-electron lasers enables structure determination from nano- and microcrystals and time-resolved molecular movies. It is close to my own interest in structure determination from very small crystals.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the proof-of-principle and methods, Fromme the photosystem work and sample development, and Hajdu the diffract-before-destroy concept. Schlichting is an equally plausible fourth contributor.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across several XFELs, though the technique depends on facilities with limited access. Chemistry impact on time-resolved reactions is still growing.
uncertainties: Limited accessibility compared with 3D electron diffraction or synchrotron serial methods.
Boundary between physics instrumentation and chemistry.
Attribution among four strong contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues opens a chemically defined therapeutic modality, with drugs in clinical trials and mechanistic insight into E3 ligases.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the PROTAC concept; Ciulli did structural and chemical work on degraders; Handa, Ito and others clarified cereblon and thalidomide mechanism. The credit is distributed and a two-part prize (PROTAC and molecular glue) may be needed.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is advancing but approvals are not yet established, so the field may be a bit early.
uncertainties: Clinical outcomes are not settled.
Compound discovery with distinct PROTAC and glue contributors.
Eight credited names make a fair three-person allocation hard.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-directed self-assembly produces discrete cages with defined cavities, enabling molecular recognition, catalysis in confined spaces and structural analysis (e.g. crystalline sponge). This is conceptually related to the 2025 coordination-network prize.
assessment.attribution: Fujita (Pd-based cages and crystalline sponge), Raymond (coordination cages and host-guest catalysis) and Nitschke (complex cage architectures) are the most defensible three, with Stang as another significant contributor.
assessment.maturity: Well established with extensive independent work, though application impact is less clear than for the higher-ranked entries and nearness to the 2025 prize may weigh against it.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2025 MOF prize and the earlier 1987 supramolecular prize.
Credit allocation including Stang and Ward.
